events.title: Russia-Ukraine war: ballistic missiles on Kyiv, energy and water sites hit
events.place: Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Kharkiv, Kyiv and nationwide
events.summary: Russian attacks killed 10 people and injured 58, including 3 children, across Ukraine in the day to 26 November, with 4 dead in Kharkiv region and 3 in Donetsk region. Ballistic missiles and 113 drones were launched overnight on 25 November; 7 people were injured at a Kyiv shopping centre, energy facilities in Odesa were struck and an attack in Mykolaiv region caused temporary blackouts in 85 settlements. Poland said on 25 November that it plans a no-fly zone near its border with Ukraine.
events.advice: Anyone in Ukraine should follow air-raid alerts and plan for power, heating and water outages as temperatures drop. Avoid non-essential travel.

events.title: US-Iran confrontation: blockade, strikes and mines in the Strait of Hormuz
events.place: Strait of Hormuz, Qeshm Island, Gulf region
events.summary: Two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on 25 and 26 November according to the UK maritime agency UKMTO, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers struck mines. A drone attack in Kuwait on 26 November, which Kuwait and Italy attributed to Iran and Iran denied, killed two Italian technicians. The US blockade of Iranian ports remains in place and the conflict is in its ninth month, with mediators from Qatar and Pakistan still passing messages.
events.advice: Avoid travel to Iran. Staff in Gulf countries should keep travel plans flexible, watch for airspace closures and follow embassy guidance.

events.title: Bahrain: Iranian missile and drone strikes
events.summary: Bahrain said an Iranian attack on 21 November hit a civilian industrial site on Sitra Island, wounding two people, one critically. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US air defence systems at two bases. Iranian strikes on Bahrain resumed on 13 November after a lull since early September.
events.advice: Staff and travellers in Bahrain should follow civil defence alerts, know their nearest shelter and expect possible flight disruption.

events.title: Gaza and West Bank: continued Israeli strikes
events.summary: Overnight Israeli strikes reported on 26 November killed two people in Deir al-Balah and three in the Shati (Beach) camp in Gaza City, according to a live news blog; the Israeli military said it killed a senior Hamas operative. Israel's defence minister threatened a new offensive if Hamas does not disarm. On 24 November Gaza's health ministry counted 1,679 people killed since the October 2025 ceasefire.
events.advice: Avoid travel to Gaza and the West Bank. Staff in Israel should follow Home Front Command instructions.
events.source: The Times of Israel, live blog 26 Nov

events.title: Lebanon: Israeli strikes continue despite truce
events.summary: The Israeli military said on 26 November that it struck rockets and launchers at Ayn al-Tina in the Beqaa Valley, with no casualties reported, after strikes on southern villages on 24 November. Lebanon's Health Ministry counts 4,390 people killed between 2 March and 5 November. Talks between Israel and Lebanon are continuing.
events.advice: Avoid southern and eastern Lebanon. Staff in Beirut should keep travel documents ready and follow embassy alerts.
events.source: The Times of Israel, live blog 26 Nov

events.title: Yemen: Saudi-led coalition strikes on Hodeidah, Saada and Amran
events.place: Hodeidah, Saada, Amran, Sanaa; western coast and Taiz
events.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said on 25 November that it struck the port of Hodeidah, after warning civilians to leave, and several targets in Saada and Amran governorates; Houthi media said Hodeidah airport was also hit. No casualty figures were given. Yemen's civil war reignited in the summer and Houthi forces are reported to be about 60 km from Aden.
events.advice: Avoid all travel to Yemen. Red Sea shipping and flights in the area may be disrupted.

events.title: Sudan: deadly drone strikes in Blue Nile state
events.place: Damazin and Roseires, Blue Nile state; Khartoum
events.summary: Drone strikes attributed to the Rapid Support Forces killed 19 civilians and wounded about 20 in Damazin and Roseires on 24 November, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. Drone attacks on Khartoum were reported on 23 November, in a civil war now in its fourth year.
events.advice: Avoid all travel to Sudan.

events.title: Eastern DR Congo: mass displacement in South Kivu
events.summary: More than 320,000 people were displaced in South Kivu in a single week in early November, and over 7 million are displaced nationwide. Fighting in Ituri is also disrupting the Ebola response.
events.advice: Avoid travel to eastern DR Congo. See the separate Ebola entry for health precautions.

events.title: Sahel: jihadist attacks in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger
events.summary: Conflict data for 7 to 13 November show an escalation by JNIM and the FLA in Mali, roadside bombs on a national route in Burkina Faso, and attacks in Niger that displaced thousands in Kirtachi.
events.advice: Avoid travel outside capital cities and follow embassy guidance in Bamako, Ouagadougou and Niamey.

events.title: Haiti: heavy fighting in Port-au-Prince
events.summary: Armed forces launched an operation on 19 November to retake the Martissant corridor of Port-au-Prince from gangs, the first major push there in five years. Police said 54 suspected gang members had been killed in the Martissant operations, according to a 24 November report, up from 34 on the first day. Around 2,500 Salvadoran troops are also deployed.
events.advice: Avoid travel to Haiti. Flights to Port-au-Prince can be suspended at short notice.

events.title: South Sudan: pre-election risk and humanitarian need
events.summary: A warning issued on 10 November flags risks ahead of elections scheduled for 22 December. About 10 million people need aid, with drought in Eastern Equatoria and flooding in Upper Nile.
events.advice: Reconsider travel around the 22 December vote.

events.title: Ethiopia: Tigray violence and tension with Eritrea
events.summary: Amnesty International said artillery strikes by Ethiopian forces and allied militia on urban areas of Tigray this year should be investigated as possible war crimes, and accused the TPLF of endangering civilians in fighting for Alamata in September, according to a 24 November roundup. Crisis Group earlier reported that relations between Addis Ababa and Asmara worsened sharply in October.
events.advice: Avoid travel to Tigray and monitor before travelling elsewhere in northern Ethiopia. No change for Addis Ababa at this stage.

events.title: Libya: aftermath of the sinking of a Russian warship
events.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died on 24 November of wounds from the Ukrainian drone attack that sank a Russian warship at a port in eastern Libya on 22 November. The Libyan National Army confirmed the deaths and said it would retaliate against Ukraine, without giving details.
events.advice: Avoid port areas in eastern Libya. Maritime traffic in the central Mediterranean may see added security measures.

events.title: France: public-service strike called for 1 December
events.summary: Eight public-service unions have called a national strike and rallies on Tuesday 1 December over pay, covering state, local-authority and hospital staff. As of 26 November neither SNCF nor RATP had announced a strike day: metro and buses are expected to run, RER lines may be affected, and SNCF forecasts are due from 17:00 on Monday 30 November. Professional firefighters are also called to strike on Friday 4 December.
events.advice: Check SNCF and RATP forecasts from 17:00 on Monday 30 November and avoid demonstration routes, where metro stations may close. Parents should expect possible school and canteen closures.

events.title: Cuba: energy collapse and shortages
events.summary: Cuba faces a humanitarian and energy crisis following US fuel restrictions in place since January, with a seventh nationwide blackout on 18 September affecting about 9.4 million people. On 24 November the head of the World Health Organization called for the restrictions to be lifted, saying they harm children and the most vulnerable.
events.advice: Expect power, fuel and connectivity outages. Travellers should carry essentials and confirm accommodation has backup power.

events.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, international health emergency
events.place: Ituri, North Kivu and six other provinces
events.summary: Declared on 15 May. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported on 26 November a total of 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths in DR Congo across 8 provinces, with community transmission continuing; WHO had counted 11,613 cases and 5,678 deaths as of 17 November. Kenya has 9 cases with none new since 19 October and Nigeria had one imported case, and both are counting down to declaring their outbreaks over. WHO confirmed on 18 November that the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern.
events.advice: Avoid travel to affected provinces. Anyone returning from eastern DR Congo or with exposure risk should follow national health authority screening rules.

events.title: Florida: largest dengue outbreak in decades
events.summary: Florida recorded 524 locally acquired dengue cases through 31 October, against 62 in all of 2025, with at least one death. Three counties have declared local emergencies, and current flooding may add mosquito breeding sites.
events.advice: Staff in Florida should use repellent and remove standing water around homes.
events.source: Center for Disaster Philanthropy, weekly update 23 Nov

events.title: Florida: record flooding on the St. Johns River
events.summary: After days of torrential rain the St. Johns River reached a record 18.68 feet, above the 1953 record. Roads are cut, rescues and evacuations are under way, and major flooding could last into December.
events.advice: Staff in affected counties should follow local evacuation orders and avoid driving through floodwater.
events.source: Center for Disaster Philanthropy, weekly update 23 Nov

events.title: US East Coast: Thanksgiving nor'easter, mass power cuts and coastal flooding
events.place: Florida to New England (map position approximate)
events.summary: The storm hit on Thanksgiving Day, 26 November: about 900,000 customers were without power that evening, and states of emergency covered all of New Jersey and southern New York including New York City. Around 400 flights were cancelled and more than 1,200 delayed by midday, water rescues were reported in Cape May, New Jersey, and flooding there was compared to Superstorm Sandy. No deaths were reported in the sources; the storm was expected to clear the New York area early on 27 November, with some outages lasting several days.
events.advice: Staff on the US East Coast should avoid flooded coastal roads, prepare for power cuts and expect flight and road delays through Friday 27 November.

events.title: Bali: floods and landslides
events.summary: Flooding that began on 22 November has killed at least two people, with one child missing. Landslides, fallen trees and building damage are reported and crews are pumping water from roads, schools and homes.
events.advice: Travellers should check road conditions and avoid river valleys and steep slopes during heavy rain.
events.source: Center for Disaster Philanthropy, weekly update 23 Nov

events.title: Indonesia: floods and landslides in West Kalimantan, Sumatra and West Java
events.summary: Flooding in Kapuas Hulu, West Kalimantan, has affected 28,875 people in 33 villages since 21 November, and 17,612 people were affected in Rokan Hilir, Riau, on 23 November. Floods and landslides hit 15 districts of Tasikmalaya, West Java, on 23 and 24 November, killing one person.
events.advice: Expect road closures and local travel delays.

events.title: Thailand: flood alert for 15 southern provinces, prolonged flooding in the centre
events.place: Ayutthaya, Suphan Buri, Lop Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chumphon; Phatthalung
events.summary: Thailand's disaster agency put 15 southern provinces, from Prachuap Khiri Khan to Narathiwat and including Phuket, Krabi, Surat Thani and Songkhla, on alert for flash floods and landslides from 27 to 30 November as the northeast monsoon strengthens. Separately, about 121,400 people were still affected on 15 November by floods that began in September, with 89 deaths recorded.
events.advice: Travellers in southern Thailand, including Phuket and Krabi, should expect heavy rain until 30 November, avoid waterways and slopes and check transport before setting out. The disaster hotline is 1784.

events.title: Malaysia: floods and landslides in five states
events.place: Selangor, Perak, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka
events.summary: Authorities report flooding and landslides across five states at the start of the monsoon season. No casualty figures are given in the source.
events.advice: Watch local weather warnings, especially for road travel outside Kuala Lumpur.

events.title: California: king tides and coastal flooding
events.summary: The San Francisco tide gauge reached 8.23 feet on the morning of 24 November, breaking a record set in 1982, according to the National Weather Service. King tides combined with an atmospheric river keep a coastal flood threat along the whole California coast until Friday 27 November, easing gradually in the Bay Area.
events.advice: Minor impact. Avoid low-lying coastal roads and car parks at high tide.

events.title: M7.2 earthquake in the Banda Sea
events.summary: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake about 125 km deep struck the Banda Sea on 21 November, with shaking felt in Maluku, Tanimbar and Dili. It follows another strong quake in the same area on 16 November.
events.advice: No major damage is reported in the source. Staff in eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste should expect aftershocks.

events.title: M6.5 earthquake near Vanuatu
events.summary: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck on 23 November at a depth of about 600 km. No tsunami warning was issued and no casualties were immediately reported.
events.advice: No action needed.

events.title: M6.4 earthquake in the Mauritius-Réunion region
events.summary: GDACS lists a magnitude 6.4 earthquake at 10 km depth in the Mauritius-Réunion region on 24 November at 11:06 UTC. The overall alert level is green, meaning low expected humanitarian impact.
events.advice: No action needed unless local authorities issue warnings.

events.title: Nigeria: large wildfires
events.place: Location not specified in alert (map position approximate)
events.summary: GDACS lists two forest fires in Nigeria updated on 24 November, covering about 48,000 and 14,700 hectares.
events.advice: Seasonal fires. Smoke may affect air quality locally.

events.title: Kuwait: deadly drone attack on an air-defence site
events.place: Kuwait (site not named by the source; approximate position)
events.summary: A drone attack on an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait on 26 November killed two Italian technicians working for a defence contractor and wounded a Kuwaiti officer and a Pakistani national. Kuwait and Italy attributed the attack to Iran, which denied involvement. Kuwait had activated its air defences against drones on 18 November, the first time since early September.
events.advice: Employees and travellers in Kuwait should follow official alerts, know where to shelter, stay away from military and energy sites and keep travel plans flexible in case of airspace closures.

events.title: Saudi Arabia: Houthi missile and drone attacks on Riyadh and ports
events.summary: On 26 November the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, two drones over the Eastern Province, a cruise missile in the west and a drone near Jeddah port, while a projectile caused minor damage at Jazan port. The Houthis said they hit Jeddah and Jazan ports in retaliation for strikes on Hodeidah, and on 25 November claimed an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery, where the coalition said four drones were intercepted. A strike on a tower in Riyadh on 24 November wounded 11 people, the second hit there in a week.
events.advice: Staff and travellers in Saudi Arabia should follow civil defence alerts and shelter when warnings sound. Check embassy advice and flight status before travelling, as some airlines have reduced or suspended services.

events.title: Ecuador: El Niño rains, floods and landslides
events.place: Coastal provinces, mainly Guayas, Esmeraldas, El Oro, Los Ríos and Manabí (approximate position)
events.summary: Ecuador's risk management agency counted 30 deaths, 15 injuries and more than 121,000 people affected by El Niño rains as of 26 November, with the latest deaths on 25 November. A nationwide red alert has been in force since 29 August; about 30,000 homes have been affected and more than 50 bridges damaged. Local elections are due on 29 November.
events.advice: Travellers should check road and bridge conditions before overland trips, especially on the coast, and avoid riverbanks and steep slopes during heavy rain.
